html:
On the 3000 BCE map, Aboriginal tribes covers the whole of mainland Australia, home to hundreds of Aboriginal peoples who had already lived there for tens of thousands of years. Its chart bar is Aboriginal Australian societies.

People reached Australia at least 50,000 years ago, among the oldest sea crossings anywhere. Burials at Lake Mungo are over 40,000 years old; see Mungo Man. By 3000 BCE groups spoke hundreds of languages and lived by hunting, fishing and gathering, with skills fitted to deserts, rivers, coasts and rainforests. They burned the land in careful patterns, fire-stick farming, to renew grass and draw game. At Budj Bim in Victoria, the Gunditjmara built stone channels and weirs to trap eels, some of them thousands of years old.

Around this time new small stone tools spread across the continent, and the dingo arrived from Asia by about 1500 BCE. The same way of life carries through the later maps as Australian Aboriginal hunter-gatherers.
sum: On the 3000 BCE map, Aboriginal tribes covers the whole of mainland Australia, home to hundreds of Aboriginal peoples who had already lived there for tens of thousands of years. Its chart bar is Aboriginal Australian societies.
